verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 22.59
verses.english: Linked Discourses 22.59

verses.pali: 6. Upayavagga
verses.english: 6. Involvement

verses.pali: Anattalakkhaṇasutta
verses.english: The Characteristic of Not-Self

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṁ viharati isipatane migadāye.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Varanasi, in the deer park at Isipatana.

verses.pali: Tatra kho bhagavā pañcavaggiye bhikkhū āmantesi:
verses.english: There the Buddha addressed the group of five mendicants:

verses.pali: “bhikkhavo”ti.
verses.english: “Mendicants!”

verses.pali: “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
verses.english: “Venerable sir,” they replied.

verses.pali: Bhagavā etadavoca:
verses.english: The Buddha said this:

verses.pali: “Rūpaṁ, bhikkhave, anattā.
verses.english: “Mendicants, form is not-self.

verses.pali: Rūpañca hidaṁ, bhikkhave, attā abhavissa, nayidaṁ rūpaṁ ābādhāya saṁvatteyya, labbhetha ca rūpe:
verses.english: For if form were self, it wouldn’t lead to affliction. And you could compel form:

verses.pali: ‘evaṁ me rūpaṁ hotu, evaṁ me rūpaṁ mā ahosī’ti.
verses.english: ‘May my form be like this! May it not be like that!’

verses.pali: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, rūpaṁ anattā, tasmā rūpaṁ ābādhāya saṁvattati, na ca labbhati rūpe:
verses.english: But because form is not-self, it leads to affliction. And you can’t compel form:

verses.pali: ‘evaṁ me rūpaṁ hotu, evaṁ me rūpaṁ mā ahosī’ti.
verses.english: ‘May my form be like this! May it not be like that!’

verses.pali: Vedanā anattā.
verses.english: Feeling is not-self …

verses.pali: Vedanā ca hidaṁ, bhikkhave, attā abhavissa, nayidaṁ vedanā ābādhāya saṁvatteyya, labbhetha ca vedanāya:
‘evaṁ me vedanā hotu, evaṁ me vedanā mā ahosī’ti.
Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, vedanā anattā, tasmā vedanā ābādhāya saṁvattati, na ca labbhati vedanāya:
‘evaṁ me vedanā hotu, evaṁ me vedanā mā ahosī’ti.
Saññā anattā …pe…
verses.english: Perception is not-self …

verses.pali: saṅkhārā anattā.
verses.english: Choices are not-self …

verses.pali: Saṅkhārā ca hidaṁ, bhikkhave, attā abhavissaṁsu, nayidaṁ saṅkhārā ābādhāya saṁvatteyyuṁ, labbhetha ca saṅkhāresu:
‘evaṁ me saṅkhārā hontu, evaṁ me saṅkhārā mā ahesun’ti.
Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā anattā, tasmā saṅkhārā ābādhāya saṁvattanti, na ca labbhati saṅkhāresu:
‘evaṁ me saṅkhārā hontu, evaṁ me saṅkhārā mā ahesun’ti.
Viññāṇaṁ anattā.
verses.english: Consciousness is not-self.

verses.pali: Viññāṇañca hidaṁ, bhikkhave, attā abhavissa, nayidaṁ viññāṇaṁ ābādhāya saṁvatteyya, labbhetha ca viññāṇe:
verses.english: For if consciousness were self, it wouldn’t lead to affliction. And you could compel consciousness:

verses.pali: ‘evaṁ me viññāṇaṁ hotu, evaṁ me viññāṇaṁ mā ahosī’ti.
verses.english: ‘May my consciousness be like this! May it not be like that!’

verses.pali: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṁ anattā, tasmā viññāṇaṁ ābādhāya saṁvattati, na ca labbhati viññāṇe:
verses.english: But because consciousness is not-self, it leads to affliction. And you can’t compel consciousness:

verses.pali: ‘evaṁ me viññāṇaṁ hotu, evaṁ me viññāṇaṁ mā ahosī’ti.
verses.english: ‘May my consciousness be like this! May it not be like that!’

verses.pali: Taṁ kiṁ maññatha, bhikkhave,
verses.english: What do you think, mendicants?

verses.pali: rūpaṁ niccaṁ vā aniccaṁ vā”ti?
verses.english: Is form permanent or impermanent?”

verses.pali: “Aniccaṁ, bhante”.
verses.english: “Impermanent, sir.”

verses.pali: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
verses.english: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

verses.pali: “Dukkhaṁ, bhante”.
verses.english: “Suffering, sir.”

verses.pali: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
verses.english: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:

verses.pali: ‘etaṁ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti?
verses.english: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”

verses.pali: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
verses.english: “No, sir.”

verses.pali: “Vedanā …
verses.english: “Is feeling permanent or impermanent?” …

verses.pali: saññā …
verses.english: “Is perception permanent or impermanent?” …

verses.pali: saṅkhārā …
verses.english: “Are choices permanent or impermanent?” …

verses.pali: viññāṇaṁ niccaṁ vā aniccaṁ vā”ti?
verses.english: “Is consciousness permanent or impermanent?”

verses.pali: “Aniccaṁ, bhante”.
verses.english: “Impermanent, sir.”

verses.pali: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
verses.english: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

verses.pali: “Dukkhaṁ, bhante”.
verses.english: “Suffering, sir.”

verses.pali: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
verses.english: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:

verses.pali: ‘etaṁ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti?
verses.english: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”

verses.pali: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
verses.english: “No, sir.”

verses.pali: “Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, yaṁ kiñci rūpaṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṁ vā sukhumaṁ vā hīnaṁ vā paṇītaṁ vā yaṁ dūre santike vā, sabbaṁ rūpaṁ: ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
verses.english: “So you should truly see any kind of form at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all form—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

verses.pali: Yā kāci vedanā atītānāgatapaccuppannā ajjhattā vā bahiddhā vā …pe… yā dūre santike vā, sabbā vedanā: ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
verses.english: Any kind of feeling at all …

verses.pali: Yā kāci saññā …pe…
verses.english: Any kind of perception at all …

verses.pali: ye keci saṅkhārā atītānāgatapaccuppannā ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā …pe… ye dūre santike vā, sabbe saṅkhārā: ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
verses.english: Any kind of choices at all …

verses.pali: Yaṁ kiñci viññāṇaṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṁ vā sukhumaṁ vā hīnaṁ vā paṇītaṁ vā yaṁ dūre santike vā, sabbaṁ viññāṇaṁ: ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
verses.english: You should truly see any kind of consciousness at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all consciousness—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

verses.pali: Evaṁ passaṁ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpasmimpi nibbindati, vedanāyapi nibbindati, saññāyapi nibbindati, saṅkhāresupi nibbindati, viññāṇasmimpi nibbindati.
verses.english: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

verses.pali: Nibbindaṁ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.
verses.english: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

verses.pali: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.
verses.english: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

verses.pali: Idamavoca bhagavā.
verses.english: That is what the Buddha said.

verses.pali: Attamanā pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinanduṁ.
verses.english: Satisfied, the group of five mendicants approved what the Buddha said.

verses.pali: Imasmiñca pana veyyākaraṇasmiṁ bhaññamāne pañcavaggiyānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ anupādāya āsavehi cittāni vimucciṁsūti.
verses.english: And while this discourse was being spoken, the minds of the group of five mendicants were freed from defilements by not grasping.

verses.pali: Sattamaṁ.
